title: Skill
description: Frontmatter schema for skill definitions under src/apothem/skills/<name>/SKILL.md. Reconciled to the live skill corpus: every shipped SKILL.md carries name, description, version, updated, archetype, userInvocable, disable-model-invocation, and allowed-tools; argument-hint is optional. The user-invocability flag is spelled userInvocable in the source corpus and user-invocable in the Claude Code emission (the claude_code install and the plugin assembler rename it); a skill carries exactly one of the two. The agnostic posture forbids a model/effort/permission preset, so effort/model/permissionMode are not admitted keys.

name.description: Human-readable kebab-case name (matches the skill folder).

description.description: Trigger-rich, capability-led description that surfaces detection signals so the harness routes matching requests to the skill. At most 1024 characters, the Agent Skills specification limit (https://agentskills.io/specification); strict consumers reject or truncate a longer one.

version.description: SemVer version of the skill definition.

updated.description: ISO 8601 date of the skill's last revision.

archetype.description: Shape class of the skill, named as a kebab-case '<class>-template' identifier (e.g. audit-template, authoring-template, workflow-template).

userInvocable.description: Source-corpus spelling: whether the operator can invoke the skill directly (false hides it from the operator's skill menu where the harness supports that).

user-invocable.description: Claude Code spelling of userInvocable (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills). The claude_code install and the plugin assembler emit it in place of userInvocable; Claude Code ignores the camelCase key.

disable-model-invocation.description: When true, the skill is reached only by explicit invocation, never auto-selected by the model from its description.

allowed-tools.description: Comma-separated tools the skill pre-approves while it runs: read-only by default. A side-effecting tool (Bash, PowerShell, Write, Edit, NotebookEdit, WebFetch) appears only as a scoped permission rule such as Bash(git log *), and the bare "*" wildcard is not accepted, because harnesses that honor this field run pre-approved tools without asking.

argument-hint.description: Optional usage hint shown to the operator describing the skill's accepted arguments and flags.

examples.name: dependency-upgrade
examples.description: Changelog-reviewed, pinned, gate-verified dependency upgrade — matched when the operator asks to 'bump deps', 'upgrade dependencies', or 'refresh dependency versions'.
